doc.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: The virtual staff in Tolliver's mind while improvising
summary: He describes a continuous imagined staff on which he places notes, and 'exploratory' playing as not playing what he practiced.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Is it possible for you to describe the thought process that is occurring when you’re improvising?

I have a staff — continuous staff — running in front of me virtually in my consciousness, and I’m sort of putting notes on there as the staff is running along, and catching those notes on the instrument. Of course this is all simultaneous, instantaneously going on. It’s a lot easier if you’ve got a slower tempo.
Whereas a breakneck speed then the brain is really firing off you know, in my case. That’s basically it. I have a virtual —
That’s fascinating. I never heard anybody describe it quite that way.

Yeah. That staff is empty until the song starts. Well the song is basically memorized to play it, you know, and then up comes the staff. But sometimes I don’t use my mind to bring the staff up. And sometimes it just shows up you know. And usually that’s when I get exploratory you know. I start rumbling with the notes you know.
Good phrase. If you had a student, if you said that to a student and they said — well why should I pretend I’m just going to say it, what do you mean by “exploratory”?
Not playing what you practiced, that you know is absolutely perfect for the chord changes.
